title: Chiral, Electronically Decoupled Layers of 1T'-WS2 Topological Insulator via Neutral-Molecule Intercalation
authors: Jiaze Xie, Fatmagül Katmer, Fang Yuan, Jaime M. Moya, Guangming Cheng, Connor J. Pollak, Xiaoyu Song, Nirmal Roy, Yakov Bloch, Moshe Ben Shalom, Jennifer Cano, Leslie M. Schoop
abstract: Monolayer 1T'-WS2 is predicted to be a two-dimensional topological insulator, but its intrinsic electronic properties are masked by strong interlayer coupling in its metallic and superconducting bulk parent phase, 2M-WS2. Isolating monolayers by mechanical exfoliation is also hindered by this coupling, preventing experimental examination of monolayer properties. Here we show that 2M-WS2 undergoes amine intercalation through a simple wet-chemical reaction, yielding superlattices in which the 1T' layers are structurally preserved but electronically decoupled by neutral molecular spacers. Intercalation expands the interlayer spacing from 0.5 to 1-4 nm and reconstructs the stacking while preserving the intralayer 1T' framework. Controlled (de)intercalation reversibly switches the system between a superconducting metal and an insulator with an activation gap matching that of the isolated monolayer. Density functional theory indicates that the electronically decoupled layers retain the nontrivial Z2 topology of the monolayer. Chiral amine intercalation further induces chiroptical activity in WS2 electronic transitions. Overall, the successful intercalation challenges the long-held view that group VIB dichalcogenides are inert toward neutral-molecule intercalation and demonstrates molecular intercalation as a general chemical route for realizing monolayer-like topological-insulator physics and enabling chiral van der Waals superlattices in bulk single crystals.
summary: The study overcomes the challenge of studying $1T'-	ext{WS}_2$ topological insulators by chemically intercalating neutral amine molecules into the bulk material. This process expands the interlayer spacing and electronically decouples the layers, allowing researchers to observe monolayer-like insulating behavior in a stable superlattice structure.
main_problem: The intrinsic topological insulator properties of monolayer $1T'-	ext{WS}_2$ are masked by strong interlayer coupling in its bulk phase, preventing direct experimental study.
main_result: Amine intercalation successfully creates superlattices where the $1T'$ layers are electronically decoupled from each other, enabling reversible switching between superconducting metal and insulating states matching monolayer behavior.
method: The researchers employed a wet-chemical amine intercalation route to structurally modify the bulk $	ext{WS}_2$ into an intercalated superlattice structure.
model_or_system: The system is based on $	ext{WS}_2$ dichalcogenides, transitioning from the metallic/superconducting $2M-	ext{WS}_2$ bulk phase to electronically decoupled, insulating superlattices via neutral-molecule intercalation.
key_observables: Interlayer spacing expansion (from 0.5 nm to 1-4 nm), electronic transition from metallic to insulating state with a measurable activation gap, and observation of chiroptical activity using chiral amines.
important_parameters: Amine spacer length/type ($	ext{R-MBA}$, $	ext{HexA}$), interlayer spacing (e.g., $17.2 \mathring{	ext{A}}$ expansion), activation gap ($20-50 	ext{ meV}$).
main_assumptions: The electronic decoupling is primarily due to the physical separation by the intercalant, allowing DFT calculations to confirm retention of the monolayer's $\mathbb{Z}_2$ topology.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate structural changes via PXRD (expanded spacing), electronic state changes via transport measurements (metal-to-insulator crossover), and optical characterization showing chiroptical effects.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the problem of interlayer coupling, presents the chemical intercalation method using amines, details structural/electronic characterizations (PXRD, transport, XPS), confirms electronic decoupling and topological retention via DFT, and concludes by establishing this as a general route for studying monolayer physics in bulk crystals.
why_interesting: This work provides an accessible chemical pathway to engineer quantum materials states (like TI behavior) that are otherwise difficult or impossible to isolate experimentally, which is highly relevant for building artificial quantum systems.

figures.caption: Fig. 1 Crystal structures and topological hierarchy of WS2. 1T′-WS2 monolayer (a), 2M- WS2 bulk (b), and amine-intercalated WS2 superlattices (c). The 1T′ monolayer is predicted to be a 2D topological insulator (TI), namely a quantum spin Hall (QSH) insulator, whereas the bilayer-based 2M bulk phase, characterized by strong interlayer coupling, experimentally shows a 3D electronic state that is metallic and superconducting. In this work, neutral amine intercalation suppresses the interlayer coupling, decoupling the stacked 1T′ layers and restoring monolayer-like electronic behavior within a translational superlattice. Schematic of reversible (de)intercalation in 2M-WS2 using MBA (a), with ex situ PXRD tracking the structural evolution (b). Pawley refinement of WS2(rac-MBA)0.5 confirms the intercalated phase (c). Raman (d), W 4f XPS (e), and DSC (f) collectively evidence the intercalation-induced structural and electronic changes. Full characterization of all amine-intercalated phases is provided in Extended Data Fig. 2.

Fig. 4 Physical properties before and after amine intercalation in WS2, exemplified by R-MBA. Temperature-dependent resistance of 2M-WS2 and WS2(R-MBA)0.5 crystals (a); the inset highlights the low-temperature superconductivity in 2M-WS2. Magnetic susceptibilities of 2M-WS2, WS2(R-MBA)0.5, and restored 2M-WS2 after deintercalation, highlighting the changes in diamagnetic response associated with superconductivity (b). Full characterization of all amine-intercalated phases is provided in Extended Data Fig. 3. Samples were zero-field cooled (ZFC) and subsequently measured under an applied magnetic field of 5 Oe. Field-cooled (FC) results are included in Fig. S24.

Fig. 5 Topology is recovered upon intercalation. Crystal structures and corresponding orbital- projected band structures along the Γ-Y path of the monolayer (a), bilayer (b), and 1T′-WS2-NH3 superlattice (c). Topological analysis indicates that the WS2-NH3 superlattice retains the nontrivial topology of the monolayer, characterized by Z2 = 1. Band structures along the full Brillouin-zone paths are provided in Extended Data Fig. 6.
